title: AgentGuard: Runtime Verification of AI Agents
publication: Proceedings 2025 40th IEEE ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering Workshops Asew 2025
secondary_abstract: The rapid evolution to autonomous, agentic AI systems introduces significant risks due to their inherent unpredictability and emergent behaviors; this also renders traditional verification methods inadequate and necessitates a shift towards probabilistic guarantees where the question is no longer if a system will fail, but the probability of its failure within given constraints. This paper presents AgentGuard, a framework for runtime verification of Agentic AI systems that provides continuous, quantitative assurance through a new paradigm called Dynamic Probabilistic Assurance. AgentGuard operates as an inspection layer that observes an agent's raw I/O and abstracts it into formal events corresponding to transitions in a state model. It then uses online learning to dynamically build and update a Markov Decision Process (MDP) that formally models the agent's emergent behavior. Using probabilistic model checking, the framework then verifies quantitative properties in real-time.

title: A trustworthy intent-driven LLM-agent workflow with state verification for power system simulation
publication: Applied Energy
secondary_abstract: Modern power system simulation workflows, including model setup, parameter configuration, scenario construction, solver invocation, and result verification, remain heavily manual and procedurally intensive. Large language models (LLMs) offer a promising way to transform high-level engineering intents into structured and reviewable simulation workflows. Yet, as probabilistic models, LLMs may generate outputs that are incomplete, incorrectly ordered, or inconsistent with the active simulation state, posing risks to workflow reliability. This paper proposes a trustworthy intent-driven LLM-agent workflow with state verification for power system simulation. The proposed framework separates LLM-based workflow planning from solver-side execution. The LLM converts heterogeneous engineering instructions into structured and reviewable candidate workflows, while a state-verification mechanism checks workflow admissibility, state-dependency constraints, and execution evidence before solver-side results are accepted. Instead of evaluating only software executability, the proposed evaluation distinguishes planning validity from verified workflow completion, where a workflow is successful only when the executed workflow satisfies the required state conditions of the intended simulation task. A controlled benchmark on the New England 39-bus system evaluates robustness under different task-complexity levels and instruction-ambiguity variants, with ablation studies quantifying the roles of schema guidance, orchestration, and LLM backbone selection. A real-world 201-bus power system further assesses practical scalability in model preparation and N-1 contingency testing. Results show that the proposed workflow reduces low-level manual interaction, achieving approximately a 19-fold improvement in model-preparation workflow efficiency and a 4.5-fold speedup in N-1 contingency-test workflow execution.
